heroCommands.comment: Use a local model in Claude Code

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Ollama lets you download and run open AI models like Gemma on your own computer with one command. It gives you a chat in the terminal, a local REST API, and Python and JavaScript libraries, and it can connect local models to tools like Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw.
sixtySeconds.problem: Running open models usually means dealing with model files, GPU settings and inference servers. Ollama handles downloading and running models for you, so you can chat with or build on a model in minutes, with your data staying on your machine.
whoFor: Beginners who want to try open models locally
Developers building apps on a local model API
Privacy-minded users who don't want to send data to the cloud
Coding agent users who want local models
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for the easiest way to run open models on macOS, Windows or Linux. For serving many users at high throughput on GPU servers, a serving engine like vLLM may suit better.
requirements: Enough RAM or GPU memory for the model you choose

overview: After installing, running ollama prompts you to run a model or connect Ollama to agents and apps such as Claude Code, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Codex and Copilot. ollama run gemma4 downloads Gemma 4 and opens a chat; the full list of models is in the library on ollama.com.

Ollama runs a REST API on localhost port 11434 for running and managing models, and official libraries ollama-python and ollama-js wrap it. ollama launch starts a specific integration, for example ollama launch claude for Claude Code or ollama launch openclaw for a personal assistant across messaging apps.

Ollama uses llama.cpp as its backend. An official Docker image, ollama/ollama, is on Docker Hub, and a large list of community apps such as Open WebUI, LobeChat, AnythingLLM and Dify integrate with it. It is MIT licensed.

tutorial.title: Run a model and call it from your code
tutorial.useCase: Chat with Gemma 4 locally, then call it through the REST API and the Python library.

steps.title: Call the REST API
Chat from Python
steps.code:
from ollama import chat

response = chat(model='gemma4', messages=[
  {'role': 'user', 'content': 'Why is the sky blue?'},
])
print(response.message.content)

tutorial.expected: The model answers in the terminal, the API returns a JSON chat response, and the Python script prints the answer.
